## Handoff (session rebar-session-3d705fec, 2026-11-17 PST, origin/main 83ca81e709e). Not claimed, no code changed.

### Established
- REB-6995 is gone. Read-only checks: `search_issues('key = "REB-6995"')` returns `[]`, and ACLI `workitem search` answers "issue does not exist". This agrees with the run's missing `leaked.log`.
- The default-run half of AC 2 already holds on main. `7c3cb5e9a4f` (bug 5f29-9bed-5a47-4a25) marks `test_delete_permission_probe` `@pytest.mark.live` (tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py:284), and `make test` and CI run `-m "integration and not live"` (Makefile:617). The probe therefore runs only on an explicit `pytest -m live`, and a local `make verify` no longer writes to live Jira.
- Timed probe at host load 18-30, run alone: 3 rounds of the same create → poll → delete as the test, instrumented per attempt (REB-7248, REB-7249, REB-7250, all deleted). Each issue was visible on the first attempt (summary search 0.36-0.54 s). The key search returned `[]` on that first attempt in 2 of the 3 rounds while the summary search already found the issue. No failure reproduced.

### Not established
- AC 1, the cause of the recurrence, is open: no timed failing run exists. The original failure happened inside the full live group (`xdist_group("live_reconcile_e2e")`, load 25-40), with other live tests creating and searching issues at the same time.
- The poll cannot explain its own failures. `_poll_until_visible` and `_issue_exists` (test_reconcile_live_e2e.py:354-419) swallow every search exception as "not visible". A failing run therefore cannot tell 120 s of index lag apart from 120 s of rejected searches (for example rate limiting from the concurrent live group).

### Needs a human decision
Reproducing the failure means running the whole `-m live` group repeatedly under load. Every run creates and deletes many REB issues in production Jira. Which way should this go?
(1) Authorize N full `pytest -m live` runs under load, with the poll changed first to record each attempt's latency and exception text in the assertion message, so the next failure names its cause.
(2) **Land only the poll instrumentation (test-only, no live runs now), and keep this bug open until the next `-m live` failure supplies the timed evidence.**
(3) Close as `superseded` by 5f29-9bed-5a47-4a25, accepting that the opt-in-only probe may still flake.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
On 2026-11-04, a local integration-tier run on macOS at load 25-40 failed `tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py::test_delete_permission_probe` with `AssertionError: created issue REB-6995 never became index-visible`. This is the same symptom as the closed bug dutiable-shaded-honeyeater, which Gerrit 1914 fixed.

The cause of the recurrence is unknown, and the test cannot reveal it. `_issue_exists` and `_poll_until_visible` (tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py:354-419) treat every search exception as "not visible". A failing run therefore cannot tell 120 s of index lag apart from 120 s of rejected searches.

Established 2026-11-17 PST:
- REB-6995 is gone from Jira.
- The probe is `@pytest.mark.live`, so it is out of `make test`/CI (bug 5f29).
- 3 timed rounds (REB-7248, REB-7249, REB-7250) were each visible on the first attempt.

The operator decided on 2026-11-17 (see comment) to land poll logging and disposable naming, then run the probe repeatedly in production Jira, then clean up every probe-created issue from Jira and rebar before closing.

## Approach
1. **Per-attempt logging in the poll (test code only).**
   - Add `_search_outcome(client, jql, key) -> tuple[bool, str]`. It runs the fresh search and returns `(found, note)`. The note is one of:
     - `"ok N hits"` for a successful search;
     - `"error HTTP <code>: <reason/message>"` for a `urllib.error.HTTPError`, which is what `_direct_rest_post_json` raises on non-2xx (`src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira/acli_rest.py:282-289`);
     - `"error <ExcType>: <message>"` for any other exception.
   - `_issue_exists` and `_poll_until_visible` use it.
   - `_poll_until_visible` gains an optional `attempts: list[str] | None` argument. Each attempt appends `t=<s>s key: <note>; summary: <note>`. The return type stays `bool`, so the existing callers and tests keep working.
   - The probe passes a list, and its "never became index-visible" assertion message includes every attempt line.
   - No config key, env var or flag.
2. **Disposable naming (probe inputs only).** The probe's `create_issue` input becomes:
   - summary `"[rebar probe - safe to delete] DELETE-ME-d01e delete-permission probe"`, keeping the existing `DELETE_ME_MARKER`, whose only use is this line (`:304`);
   - description `"Disposable artifact of rebar's live delete-permission probe (tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py). It can, and should, be deleted if it is still present after testing finishes."`.
   - `AcliClient.create_issue` already forwards `title`/`description` (`src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py:337-355`). No shared create code changes.
3. After the change merges, from a worktree at origin/main:
   - Run `pytest -m live tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py::test_delete_permission_probe` up to 20 times, one at a time, stopping at the first failure.
   - Record each created key (from the log) and each failure's attempt lines on this ticket.
   - Then delete any surviving probe issue from Jira, and archive any rebar copy found by key or by prefix search. This includes REB-7248, REB-7249 and REB-7250.
   - Record per-key confirmation from both systems on this ticket.

## Scope
- `tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py`: `_search_outcome`, the `_issue_exists`/`_poll_until_visible` changes, the probe's summary, description and assertion message, and new offline tests.

## Testing
- New offline tests, with fake clients and the existing `_FakeClock`:
  - A client whose search raises `urllib.error.HTTPError(…, 429, "Too Many Requests", …)` makes `_poll_until_visible` return False. Every attempt line contains `error HTTP 429: Too Many Requests`.
  - A client returning `[]` records `ok 0 hits`.
  - A client visible at t=60 returns True, and its last attempt line shows `ok 1 hits`.
- A test asserts the probe's create payload summary starts with `[rebar probe - safe to delete]` and its description contains `should, be deleted`. It does this by extracting the probe's constants, so no live call is made.
- The existing poll tests still pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each poll attempt records whether "not visible" came from a successful empty search or from a search error with its HTTP status and message, and a failed probe's assertion message includes those lines. Checked by the new offline tests.
- [ ] Probe-created issues carry the disposable prefix and deletion note. Checked by the new test.
- [ ] `make verify` exits 0, and the change merges with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.
- [ ] After the merge, up to 20 live probe runs are recorded on this ticket, with every created key and any failure's attempt lines.
- [ ] Every probe-created key (including REB-7248, REB-7249 and REB-7250) is confirmed absent from Jira and from the rebar store, recorded per key on this ticket.
- [ ] The cause of the recurrence is identified from a logged failing run and fixed in a follow-up change. If no failure occurs in the bounded runs, this box stays open and so does the bug.

file_impact.reason: per-attempt poll logging (empty vs HTTP error), disposable probe naming, offline tests
